story: At 9:17 on this humid, hazy Tuesday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is bench-testing LED rope light strings at his workbench while sketching out his wiring plan. Donna is heading down Magnolia Loop with a determined stride, and Hal is watching the street through his binoculars to keep tabs on Gary's cart modifications and count Donna's flamingos. Meanwhile, Rosa is at her kitchen counter, planning tonight's dinner menu and jotting down the groceries she'll need for four.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-test the LED rope light strings on the 12V supply and sketch the wiring plan
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (hal binoculars): Scan the street to confirm Gary's cart modifications and count Donna's flamingos
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Plan the dinner menu and check what groceries I need for four people

gary.thought_process: I'm at the house, nobody around, and the bench test of the marine speaker went fine last tick. Next step is the LED rope light, so I should test it on the 12V supply before I mount anything on the cart. I keep thinking about L-01 and L-03: exterior mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, and amplified sound has quiet hours. I'll keep all of this on the bench for now and not touch the cart's exterior until the paperwork is sorted. The parade sign-up closes at the end of the month, so I've got time to do this right.

parameters.content: Bench-test the LED rope light strings on the 12V supply and sketch the wiring plan

donna.thought_process: I've already penciled in Saturday at 8 with Gary and packed the spare paddle, so the logistics are handled. Nobody's around to talk to, and it's a humid Tuesday morning. Gary's a total beginner, and a Saturday ladder match is only worth it if he's ready, so I should get him some practice before then. The rec center is where the courts are, and that's where I'll find Gary or at least book a practice slot (two hours max per L-05). Heading out the door with the bag.

parameters.content: Heading out with my paddles to find Gary and set up a practice session before Saturday.

hal.thought_process: I'm home at 9:17 AM with nobody around. I finalized my notes on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos last tick, but I haven't actually seen the carts or the flamingo count today. Rules are only worth enforcing if the facts are solid. The binoculars are right here. I'll check the street and confirm the ornament count and any cart modifications before I take the report to the review committee. Gary did admit he's wiring first and filing after, which is plain enough, but I'd rather be fair than hasty.

parameters.content: Scan the street to confirm Gary's cart modifications and count Donna's flamingos

rosa.thought_process: I've already invited Hal and blocked off an evening with no per-diem shift. I'm home alone in my kitchen, and the dinner won't happen unless I plan it. Gary, Donna, and Hal are all invited, or soon will be, and I want this to feel warm rather than rushed. The next useful step is to start on the food: decide on a menu and check what I have on hand, since I'm not in line-of-sight of anyone to talk to. Cooking is also what I do when I want to thank people.

parameters.content: Plan the dinner menu and check what groceries I need for four people

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
